conventions.convention: Use smooth, oriented, time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifolds with signature (−,+,+,+); manifold orientation and time orientation are independent.
The restricted NEC is T(k,k) ≥ 0 for the specified generator and total electromagnetic-plus-material stress; it is an adopted restriction, not a consequence of Einstein's equation.

Area monotonicity requires an affine generator flow on the entire future half-line, with persistent compact embedded spacelike cuts; the derivative formula is asserted for λ > λ₀ and monotonicity includes λ₀.
ACω means every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function; the stated calculations retain this premise without adopting full AC.
The KN family has zero magnetic flux and strict subextremality m² > a² + q². Constants G_N, c and μ₀ remain fixed during parameter differentiation; ε₀μ₀c² = 1.
Length-time normalization gives Ω_SI = cΩ_geom, κ_acc = c²κ_geom and Φ_SI = (c/α)Φ_geom. E_par = m_*c² is a family parameter, without an ADM/Komar identification or dynamical-process interpretation.

load_bearing.statement: On the strict subextremal, zero-magnetic-flux selected KN family, with fixed constants, dE_par = κ_acc c² dA_H/(8πG_N) + Ω_SI dJ + Φ_SI dQ_e and E_par = κ_acc c² A_H/(4πG_N) + 2Ω_SI J + Φ_SI Q_e. The Schwarzschild slice is included through its separate exact supplier. These are stationary-family identities, not process laws or thermodynamic identifications.

For fully supplied named smooth classical matter-model data and an admitted configuration, adopt the smooth equation-based Einstein–Maxwell equations and T(k,k) ≥ 0 on the specified smooth future null generator. The restricted area deduction additionally requires the supplied future flow and persistent compact spacelike cuts.

Under the stated smooth Einstein–Maxwell model, generator NEC, ACω, and future affine flow with persistent compact embedded spacelike cuts, θ ≥ 0 on every future cut, A_H′(λ) = ∫S_λ θ dA ≥ 0 for λ > λ₀, and A_H(λ₂) ≥ A_H(λ₁) whenever λ₂ ≥ λ₁ ≥ λ₀.

concerns.concern: The Statement calls Φ_SI = cq r_+/(αD) the voltage 'constant on the horizon cross-section and vanishing at spatial infinity'; Facts [L1] similarly says 'the potential tends to zero at spatial infinity.' As defined, Φ_SI is a family-dependent horizon value, with no spatial argument or infinity limit; for q ≠ 0 it is nonzero. The opened supplier pthm-emg-xs-kn-horizons instead specifies the infinity limit of the coefficients of the spacetime potential A_in. Distinguish that gauge-reference limit, or an explicitly defined off-horizon contraction, from its horizon value. The work-law coefficients and conversion algebra are unaffected.

seams_checked.note: Parameter maps, SI factors, strict-domain restriction and separate Schwarzschild completion agree with the opened suppliers. The infinity-limit wording in pthm-tgr-kn-family-mechanics conflates the horizon voltage with the spacetime potential whose coefficient limit the supplier actually specifies; see the presentation concern.

The opened framework definition supplies compatible signature, length coordinates, generator differentiation and κ_acc = c²κ_geom. The assigned items introduce no temperature or entropy identification.

The area theorem retains the supplier's affine future half-line, persistent compact spacelike embeddings, ACω and endpoint restrictions; Einstein contraction supplies exactly its null-convergence hypothesis. KN differential and Smarr identities preserve j = ma, strict subextremality and the separately verified Schwarzschild slice.

Opened both downstream items. They use the exact SI stationary-family differential, retain fixed constants and strict subextremality, and separately adopt reversible heat and temperature identifications. They do not infer entropy from the classical area theorem or turn the family identity into a process law.
